subject: Production: latency & error surge after model v4.2 / qv2-int8 rollout
messages:
From: Chris Langston <chris.langston@umbrapay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Production: latency & error spike after v4.2 rollout

Monica / Rishi,

We pushed your v4.2 model (qv2-int8 profile) to production at 02:00 PT this morning. Since then we've seen p95 jump from ~180ms to 460ms and p99s spiking to 1.4s — plus a small but steady increase in 5xxs (~0.6% -> 2.3%) tied to the same time window. This is blocking checkout flows for a subset of traffic (~12% of requests).

Can you confirm whether this is expected with the quant profile? We scoped the rollout to 20% traffic; the impact looks larger than that. Need immediate triage and plan to mitigate customer impact.

Attaching a small sample of traces (request_traces.log) and a p99 histogram.

Chris Langston
CTO, UmbraPay
chris.langston@umbrapay.com

Attachments: request_traces.log (text), p99_histogram.png (image)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Langston <chris.langston@umbrapay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: latency & error spike after v4.2 rollout

Chris — thank you for the quick heads-up and the artifacts. We're flagging this as P1. Initial notes from our on-call infra team: the p95/p99 jump aligns with two changes that rolled together this morning: the v4.2 model swap and the new qv2-int8 kernel selection.

Immediate actions we are taking (timeline below):
- 09:40: enabled detailed sampling on the affected hosts to capture full traces (we have your traces).
- 09:48 started traffic miter to route a subset of affected traffic to v4.1 fallback to measure delta.
- 10:05 initiated a targeted rollback for the qv2-int8 profile on the 10% of hosts showing decode stalls.

We expect the first rollback signals within 20–30 minutes; I'll update you with p95/p99 and 5xx numbers as soon as we have them.

Ask from your side: can you confirm whether the 12% of requests were in the EU/US mobile mix? That will help routing for the rollback.

I'll loop in Marissa for exec visibility if this does not materially improve within the hour.

— Monica Patel
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: p99_histogram.png, request_traces.log

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Langston <chris.langston@umbrapay.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: latency & error spike after v4.2 rollout

Chris — naturally sorry for the disruption. Monica is leading the technical remediation; I'm keeping UmbraPay leadership updated on our side. Couple quick customer-facing notes from me:
- If rollback to v4.1 reduces error/latency in the next 30–60m we'll propose a full traffic pin until we finish a deeper post-mortem.
- If you want, we can issue a one-time usage credit tied to the impacted timeframe — happy to draft language for your CFO.

Please keep Monica's thread as the single source. I'll be available on the call if you want to escalate to a short CTO-to-CTO bridge.

Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Langston <chris.langston@umbrapay.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@umbrapay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: latency & error spike after v4.2 rollout — resolution and next steps

Chris / Maya — final update and next steps.

Summary:
- 11/04 09:40 — detected p95/p99 and 5xx surge after v4.2 + qv2-int8 rollout.
- 11/04 10:05 — rolled back qv2-int8 on the small cohort of hosts showing decode stalls; routed 30% of affected traffic back to v4.1 for measurement.
- 11/04 11:15 — p95 decreased from 460ms -> 210ms; p99 dropped from 1.4s -> 260ms on the fallback segment. 5xx rate returned to baseline by 11:40.
- 11/05 — full rollback to v4.1 for production traffic while we finish root-cause analysis.

Root cause (preliminary):
- A interactions bug in the new kernel selector for qv2-int8 that mis-specified a buffer alignment case under long-context requests. In practice this produced increased memory copy + occasional decode stalls for requests >1k tokens. Quantization itself did not reduce output quality materially, but the stall pattern produced timeouts and higher tail latency.

Attachments: quant-profile-diff.txt includes the kernel selector diff and the traces we collected. Full RCA targeted for 11/10 EOD.

Customer-facing remediation plan:
1) Immediate: keep production pinned to v4.1 until RCA and a patched qv2-int8 are validated in a staging canary.
2) Short-term (next 72h): engineering will produce a constrained qv2-int8 build that disables the problematic selector and run a 2-day canary against UmbraPay's traffic mix.
3) Compensation: Rishi to propose a usage credit for the impacted window.
4) Post-mortem: 11/10 EOD - we will share the full timeline, code diffs, test coverage gaps, and mitigation steps.

We're assigning Irene & the infra team as leads for the patch; Marissa will coordinate any exec-level comms you want to share with UmbraPay board.

I'll schedule a short wrap-up call for Tuesday 11/09 09:00 PT unless you prefer a different time.

Thanks again for the quick signal — we'll get this fully documented and prevent recurrence.

— Monica Patel
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
